loop.name: session-log-driven-turn-loop
loop.what: One session's turn is a while-loop over `needsContinuation`: append turn/start + user/message, then per step claim steer inputs, append step/start, run the compaction pressure check and the budget ladder, emit agent/pre-step, derive messages FROM THE LOG (deriveMessages) and re-assert that the derived array is what the log says (assertMessagesFromLog), stream the model, append assistant/message and tool/call, execute the step's tool batch, append step/end, then turn/end. Nothing rewrites the model surface mid-stream: every surface change is a log append that precedes the step.
invariants: All context control (steer claim, compaction, budget, pre-step emit) happens at the TOP of a step, before messages are derived
The model may only ever see messages derived from the session log
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed: maxTurns exceeded throws, a model stream `error` event throws, a tool batch rethrow fails the turn; the run's final text is the last derived assistant message

loop.name: four-tier-input-admission-with-durable-inbox-projection
loop.what: Inputs enter through four tiers (send / followup / steer / inject) which differ on TWO axes: the inbox delivery class (queue vs steer) and the intent (user vs system). mapSubmitToAdmission maps send and followup to delivery:'queue', steer to delivery:'steer', and inject to steer-or-queue depending on scope 'turn'|'session' with intent 'system' plus a synthetic {description, scope}. There is no per-input 'wake' field: the executor is event-driven, so ANY admission while idle starts the idle drain and a queue admission during a turn waits for the next turn boundary, while only steer-delivery inputs are claimed at the step boundary.
invariants: Only steer-delivery inputs are claimed at the step boundary; queue inputs wait for the turn boundary
Every inbox mutation is a session-log append, so a cold resume rebuilds the pending set from the log alone
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed on admission: a duplicate pending id or a malformed admitted input throws before anything is queued

loop.name: per-session-serial-lane-with-cross-session-parallelism
loop.what: createSessionExecutor appends every submit as a pump onto ONE promise chain, so exactly one turn runs per session at a time, and each pump drains the pending FIFO to empty before releasing. Nothing is shared between executors and the registry is a plain map, so N sessions run concurrently in one process. A turn failure stops that pump (remaining pending stay for a future pump) but is captured, not propagated into the chain, and is re-thrown by drain() so one place observes it.
invariants: Two turns on the same session never overlap
A pump rejection must never unwrap the lane chain (later submits must still pump)
loop.failurePolicy: fail-soft internally / fail-loud at drain(): a failed turn stops that pump, the error is stored and re-thrown by drain(); the chain continues for later submits

loop.name: ordered-tool-batch-commit-lane-with-bounded-concurrency
loop.what: Tool calls are collected during the model stream and executed only after it ends, by a bounded rolling pool: a group is a maximal run of concurrency-safe calls (an exclusive call is a singleton group that never overlaps), only the tool body (dispatch) overlaps while prepare and finalize run in the ordered lane, and commit order is enforced by a head-of-line cursor so the log order is the model's order independent of completion order.
invariants: Prepare and finalize never overlap; only the tool body may
Commit order equals model order, enforced by the head-of-line cursor
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed, throw-fails-turn: stop starting, drain started calls, rethrow the first error with NO fabricated results for unstarted calls; an abort dominates a coincident failure by giving started-but-unsettled slots a synthetic fill so settled siblings still commit real results

loop.name: three-layer-overflow-ladder-compact-reset-fail-closed
loop.what: enforceBudget runs at every step boundary after the compaction pressure check: if checkBudget is not ok it (1) runs the compaction engine's compact, (2) if the compactor exists AND budget.resetWindow is not false, runs a pure resetWindow keeping the last resetRetainLast events, (3) throws `prompt_too_long`. Layer 2 is reachable only when a compaction engine exists (guard `if (compactor && resetAllowed)`), so a budget-only agent goes straight from a failed compaction to fail-closed. Budget config is validated loudly at createAgent because a NaN contextWindow made every comparison false and silently killed the whole ladder.
invariants: Budget config is validated at construction (finite positive contextWindow, non-negative integer resetRetainLast/overheadTokens)
The host-known overhead (system prompt + tool schemas) is added to every boundary measurement
loop.failurePolicy: mixed by layer: layers 1-2 are fail-soft (compaction never throws by contract), layer 3 is fail-closed (throws `prompt_too_long`)

loop.name: abort-semantics-threaded-to-the-transport
loop.what: Cancellation is checked at two points in the loop (before a step and on every streamed event) and the turn's AbortSignal is additionally placed on the LLM request so cancel reaches the transport, because the loop can only observe an abort when an event ARRIVES and a provider parked on a silent socket would otherwise be unstoppable. The executor keeps a per-input signal map so a turn is cancellable through the lane, and inbox.cancel marks an admitted input cancelled.
invariants: The abort signal rides the LLM request, not only the loop's event checks
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed: an observed abort throws `agent aborted` out of the turn

loop.name: one-assembly-two-hosts-single-flight-get-or-create
loop.what: createSessionAssembly is the single per-session environment builder shared by the one-shot headless run, the multi-turn web service, the TUI, the SDK and ACP servers; it resolves the model BEFORE mounting anything, disposes the half-built assembly on a failed mount and rethrows, and disposes in reverse mount order best-effort. createSessionService wraps it with a single-flight getOrCreate per session id (one shared creation promise, hooks fire once inside it), a two-layer-paced submit with a stable public row id, and a queue projection that merges service-front and lane rows by that id.
invariants: No partial assembly escapes: a failed mount disposes what it built and rethrows
Model policy defaults to production-safe 'required'; a mock client is only built when the caller explicitly opts into 'test-mock'
The assembly disposes what it mounted but NEVER closes the coordinator or the telemetry stream
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed at the boundaries (missing model throws ModelUnavailableError, submit on a closed service rejects, an unknown task id throws) and fail-open only for teardown (every unmount is individually caught and never throws)

loop.name: durable-restore-without-re-append
loop.what: The durable session loader copies a restored session's events into the live mirror WITHOUT running append hooks and attaches the coordinator write-behind only to NEW live events, so a resume is a pure replay rather than a re-append of the whole history; turn/end triggers a flush. Resume also restores the lineage header (delegationDepth/origin/parentSession) because the subagent depth guard reads it and without it a resumed session would present as root-depth.
invariants: Restored history is never re-mirrored; only new events are new
loop.failurePolicy: fail-closed: a resume-load failure returns a clean exitCode 1 result rather than an unhandled rejection before the run starts

session.name: append-only-event-log-with-seq-by-append
session.what: The session is an append-only event log; append assigns `seq = session.events.length` itself, so an event that arrives with seq undefined can never be hidden by ANY mechanism. Every removal is expressed as a projection marker rather than a rewrite, which is what makes a resumed session a pure replay of the log.
invariants: The raw log is never rewritten or truncated
Unkeyed events (seq undefined) are permanently visible
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed at the write boundary (append throws on a foreign source on assistant/message packages and on non-canonical base64 / unsupported media type / oversize images) and deliberately fail-safe on read (every projection degrades on malformed persisted events)

session.name: derivemessages-wire-shape-enforcement
session.what: deriveMessages is the single model-visible projection and it enforces the wire shape of a step as one unit: tool/call events are buffered and flushed as assistant(content, toolCalls) followed by the tool results (never interleaved), the step's assistant/message folds INTO the same assistant message, a mid-step user/message is deferred until after that block, and step/end flushes so consecutive steps never merge into role-alternation-breaking runs.
invariants: Function call blocks always precede their outputs
Role alternation is preserved across step boundaries
session.failurePolicy: read-side fail-safe: malformed persisted shapes (e.g. a truthy non-array output.images) must not throw out of the projection

session.name: jsonl-backend-with-atomic-rewrite-and-torn-tail-recovery
session.what: One file per session: header line 0 (JSON SessionMeta) plus one JSON event per line. Parsing takes the contiguous committed prefix and stops at the first unparsable line while a separate probe detects a torn final line; every whole-file rewrite is temp file (wx) + write + fsync + rename with best-effort directory fsync, and an append writes at the committed byte offset and on failure truncates back to the previous committed size so a clean retry cannot duplicate seqs. This backend owns STRUCTURAL repair (truncate + synthetic closers); the semantic tool-result repair lives in session-persistence.
invariants: Path safety is enforced in one artifactPath helper: a posix-absolute id, a win32-rooted id or a path resolving outside the store root is rejected
updateMeta replaces ONLY line 0 and keeps every event line byte-exact
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed on writes (append failure rolls back and rethrows, create uses flag wx, an out-of-root id throws) and tolerant on reads (a torn tail truncates to the committed prefix)

session.name: coordinator-load-gate-version-refusal-before-repair
session.what: load reads the file, runs assertVersionSupported (refuse newer-than-build; refuse a hole in the upgrade chain) and only THEN calls backend.repair, because read is non-destructive while repair may truncate and rewrite. The same gate refuses unknown event types unless they carry ignorable:true (deprecated and dropped) or were registered via registerEventType; the package registers its own set of new event types at module init so a persistence-only path still loads team/*, todo/write, goal/change, job/status, schedule/change, agent/input/*, session/title, plan/mode, subagent/*, reasoning, command/* and rewind/point. rewind/point is deliberately NOT ignorable because dropping it would silently resurrect rewound turns.
invariants: The one operation that can destroy data must be unreachable for a file this build does not understand
Hide-markers are never treated as ignorable
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed: unsupported/newer format and a missing upgrade path throw SessionFormatUnsupportedError; an unknown non-ignorable event type is refused

session.name: write-behind-with-failure-retention-and-quiescence-barrier
session.what: Appends are batched to the backend by fixed-deadline write-behind: on a failed write the batch is put back at the FRONT of the queue and the automatic timer is paused until new work arrives, so a background failure neither loses events nor spins. flush() cancels the wait and drains through a barrier that never rejects the producer, because a producer must not be failed by durability it did not await.
invariants: A failed batch is re-queued ahead of newer events (no reordering)
flush() never rejects its caller
session.failurePolicy: fail-soft by design: background flush failures go to reportBackgroundFailure, documents report but never reject the caller, close() is best-effort allSettled

session.name: tail-only-log-semantic-crash-repair
session.what: A PURE, DETERMINISTIC, TAIL-ONLY repair layer above the backend's structural repair adds a synthetic TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH tool/result for every unmatched tool/call in the LAST turn and closes an open step/turn. Earlier turns are never touched and the input array is never mutated, keeping the raw log replayable byte-for-byte. Without it a crash mid-tool replays assistant(toolCalls) with no tool responses, which breaks Messages-API alternation on continue.
invariants: Repair is tail-only and pure (no input mutation)
A synthetic result is marked as aborted-before-dispatch, never as a fabricated success
session.failurePolicy: fail-soft / integrity-preserving: repair only adds closers and markers; nothing is deleted

session.name: session-ownership-lease-os-byte-range-lock
session.what: One process holds a process-lifetime EXCLUSIVE OS byte-range lock on a per-session lock file (Win32 LockFileEx via koffi / Linux flock), acquired non-blocking with a JS backoff retry until a deadline, released idempotently. The OS auto-releases on process death so there is no stale-lock problem; the lock path is derived only from the session id as <storeRoot>/.i-harness-locks/<sha256(sessionId).slice(0,24)>.lock. Only win32 and linux ship bindings; any other platform (including darwin) fails closed with SessionLockUnsupportedError and no weaker lockfile+PID fallback is shipped.
invariants: Non-blocking at the OS level; the wait lives in JS
No weaker fallback is shipped for unsupported platforms
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed throughout: a live conflicting holder past the deadline throws SessionLockConflictError, an unsupported platform or missing native backend throws SessionLockUnsupportedError, any non-conflict OS failure throws immediately

session.name: fork-with-source-coordinate-marker-remapping
session.what: Fork seeds a child session with a completed-turn prefix from the source and applies the SOURCE's own hidden-region semantics in the child's coordinate space: rewind windows are extended back to the anchor turn's turn/start, rewind/point markers are DROPPED (a copied marker would assert a phantom cut over events the child never had), compaction markers are KEPT, and the kept events are renumbered with shadowedSeqs/removedSeqs/messageSeqs remapped. The child therefore sees exactly what the parent's model saw.
invariants: Markers are never copied verbatim across a coordinate change
Only complete turns are copied (completed-turn prefix)
session.failurePolicy: fail-closed: SessionForkUnavailableError when the backend cannot support the fork

session.name: session-listing-blank-probe-and-title-projection
session.what: Session discovery is served by the JSONL backend's list/profile surface plus session-title: profile() is honest-bounding rather than exact (an artifact at or under 1024 bytes is read whole for the exact blank answer; a larger one is served blank:false WITHOUT reading the body, and its header is read from a capped 64 KiB window on line 0). Titles come from session-title, which appends a session/title event (latest-wins projection) and mirrors a namespaced document for cheap list screens.
invariants: The blank probe never guesses: 'may have content', never 'is blank'
Only real user messages are eligible title inputs (any user/message carrying a source is excluded)
session.failurePolicy: fail-soft: provider title suggestion degrades to a deterministic word-count fallback, and the document mirror write is fired-and-caught

context.name: single-projection-token-accounting
context.what: token-meter prices exactly deriveMessages(session) — what the model actually sees — and never touches raw events, so shadowed (compaction/reset), rewound and pruned events cost nothing automatically with no second hiding implementation. Estimation is fixed-density: chars/4 with per-message role overhead, per-block overhead, per-tool-call name+args pricing and a flat per-image estimate; the budget is floor(contextWindow * reserveRatio) and overflow happens only when tokens STRICTLY exceed it.
invariants: Any measurement other than the derived projection would make the budget gate wrong exactly when it matters
overheadTokens (system prompt + tool schemas, which the log never carries) is added to every measurement
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed on parameters (checkBudget throws on a reserveRatio outside (0,1] or a non-integer overheadTokens) while the measurement itself is not defensive — callers wrap it

context.name: append-only-shadow-projection-compaction-never-rewrites-the-log
context.what: Hiding is expressed entirely as markers — compaction/summary.shadowedSeqs, compaction/reset.removedSeqs and rewind/point windows — and deriveMessages does one pre-pass collecting the shadow set plus the melded rewind cuts, then a render pass whose skip test is the UNION (`ev.seq !== undefined && (shadowed.has(ev.seq) || hideByRewind(ev.seq))`). A rewind therefore never un-shadows a compaction's removed seqs, and the reset path deliberately appends a marker instead of truncating because the persistence backends are append-only: an in-place deletion never reached disk and the deleted history returned on every resume. Pruning is NOT part of that skip union — derivePruneSubstitutes(session) is a SUBSTITUTE map applied to the tool/result CONTENT during the render pass, i.e. a third, different hiding shape (replace, not skip).
invariants: The durable log is never rewritten; resume is a pure replay
Unkeyed events (seq undefined) are never removable
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft at runtime: a failed compaction warns and returns {compacted:false} to be retried on the next step; every bound is validated fail-loud at config resolve time

context.name: auto-compaction-gate-stack-with-hysteresis-and-breaker
context.what: The AUTO path is a documented gate stack: (1) a pressure gate that includes overheadTokens, (2) sticky state set by an auto success that still leaves the surface over threshold, (3) a re-fire guard (no new non-marker events since the last compaction/end), (4) hysteresis via minTurnsBeforeRecompact turn/end events, (5) a breaker after 3 consecutive auto failures where new content releases the pause but only a success resets the counter. Explicit compact() is UNGATED and its success is the other release condition.
invariants: Each gate exists to stop a specific hot loop (sticky covers the prune-only pass, which appends no compaction/end)
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a summarizer throw (including a degenerate-output throw after ONE same-model retry below minSummaryChars) warns and returns {compacted:false}; only config resolution is fail-loud

context.name: model-free-prune-pass-auto-path-only
context.what: A plan of every tool/result whose stringified output exceeds thresholdChars (head 4096 / tail 1024 carving, middle byte count recorded) is priced against the visible surface, and if the substitute surface alone falls under the threshold the pass appends the prune marker and returns compacted:true with NO model call. Explicit compact() always summarizes, because an explicit user-requested compact must do what was asked.
invariants: Prune is available only on the auto path
A pruned event renders as its substitute, so the summary-input surface drops the image bytes (v0 carve; image-aware summarize is deferred)
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a prune stringify failure degrades to 'not prunable'

context.name: anchored-incremental-summarization-with-verbatim-sensitive-instructions
context.what: Anchoring is a PROMPT property, not an event-shape change: the last compaction/summary text is injected in a <previous-summary> block and the model is told to UPDATE rather than restate, and imperative shadow lines matching a marker list are prefilled VERBATIM into a Sensitive Instructions section (the marker match is only a flag; the original wording is never reworded or dropped). Each round still appends its own summary event carrying that round's shadowedSeqs.
invariants: User instructions are never paraphrased into the summary
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft: the summarizer's failure path is the engine's {compacted:false} path

context.name: compaction-engine-is-not-wired-in-any-shipped-host-inert
context.what: The append-only compaction engine is reachable through exactly one dependency edge and no shipped host supplies it. createAgent builds a compactor ONLY when deps.compact exists, and its compact() otherwise returns {compacted:false, shadowedSeqs:[]}. In createSessionAssembly the compactor config is passed only when opts.compact !== undefined; in createSessionService the modelBindingFor path computes `binding.contextWindow === undefined || opts.compact === undefined ? undefined : {...}` — note the condition is a DISJUNCTION, so a supplied compact config is ALSO dropped whenever the binding carries no contextWindow. There are exactly FIVE non-test createSessionService call sites and NONE passes compact: packages/tui/src/backend/embedded.ts:969-980, apps/tui/src/index.ts:235-240, apps/cli/src/index.ts:424-441 (sdk server), apps/cli/src/index.ts:594-606 (acp server) and apps/cli/src/web.ts:471-500, and the headless path (apps/cli/src/run.ts, the only non-test createSessionAssembly caller) reads opts.compact which NOTHING sets — no host flag and no setting populates HeadlessOptions.compact (only the TUI layout boolean and internal pass-throughs use the name elsewhere). Net effect in this build: auto-compaction never fires and /compact answers 'No compactable history yet.' (or the TUI's 'compact: backend seam absent' toast). The budget ladder IS wired, so an over-long session reaches the fail-closed `prompt_too_long` instead of being compacted.
invariants: compact() with no engine is a no-op, never a throw
Layer 2 (resetWindow) is unreachable without an engine, so the ladder degrades to fail-closed
context.failurePolicy: fail-soft at the seam (a no-op result), whose practical consequence is the fail-closed budget throw one layer up

context.name: runtime-context-as-durable-log-snapshots
context.what: Dynamic context goes into the LOG, not the system prompt: each named section is rendered at agent/pre-step and appended as a plugin-sourced user/message ONLY when the rendered text changed, so it is model-visible, replayable and durable through the session's own coordinator mirror. An empty render appends the explicit RUNTIME_CONTEXT_CLEARED notice so 'nothing applies any more' is itself a value that dedupes and voids earlier snapshots. On create the service scans the log backwards for the last snapshot from this package and adopts its text, so a resumed session keeps the same snapshot without re-appending; snapshots are marked internal:true (model-visible, not a user turn).
invariants: Snapshot changes are change-only appends; an unchanged render appends nothing
The cleared notice is the representable empty state
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed only on duplicate section names; the render path has no try/catch, so a failing section getter or an invalid append propagates

constants.name: RUNTIME_CONTEXT_CLEARED
constants.value: "Current runtime context: none. Earlier runtime-context snapshots no longer apply."

context.name: instruction-file-discovery-with-a-sync-stat-keyed-cache
context.what: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md are discovered global-first then workspace ancestors root->workspace so the closest file renders LAST (most salient), with at most ONE candidate per directory (AGENTS.md preferred over CLAUDE.md) and a search in ~ and ~/.claude. The section is rendered with a per-file `### <workspace-relative path>` header, joined blank-line separated and hard-capped with a `(truncated)` suffix. The getter is SYNCHRONOUS because the runtime-context pre-step render seam is sync, and it caches by (file list | max mtimeMs | total size) so an unchanged tree costs one stat per file per step boundary.
invariants: At most one instruction file per directory contributes
Rendered order is the only salience signal a text section has
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed on real read errors (anything that is not ENOENT/ENOTDIR rethrows) and fail-open on stat (a statSync failure is swallowed and falls through to a full re-read next call)

context.name: two-layer-output-retention-and-spill
context.what: Output-size control has two layers: a pure byte-budget text retainer that keeps a head and/or tail without splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs (head prefix found by binary search plus a back-off walk; tail walks backwards treating pairs atomically), and a spill store that writes the COMPLETE original outside the workspace (per-process mkdtemp root or a configured stable root) and answers a notice string with the file path. spill-guard composes both as a registry-level cascade handler on tools/execute; the label is injectively encoded before entering the filename and the file is opened 'wx' at mode 0o600.
invariants: headBytes + tailBytes === maxBytes < fullBytes (the pieces are provably disjoint)
A spilled original is never written inside the workspace
context.failurePolicy: mixed and explicit: option validation is fail-loud, spill writing is fail-loud, GC is fail-open (failures only console.warn and never block the mount)

context.name: context-window-resolution-chain
context.what: The effective context window is a per-field chain: explicit user value > profile.modelContexts[modelId] > profile.contextWindow > the value-only model-catalog card > undefined, with maxOutputTokens coming from the card/user maxTokens. A run with no window knowledge anywhere returns undefined, and consumers gate on it fail-closed (no window => no budget ladder, and the compact pass-through stays exactly as the caller wrote it). The compaction engine resolves catalog-first the same way, and the effective policy is a per-model overlay on the global chain keyed by exact 'provider/model' with malformed keys failing loud at resolve.
invariants: A card fills a missing value but NEVER overwrites an explicit one
The card is value-only and never provides a request default
context.failurePolicy: fail-closed: an unknown protocol throws at build, a malformed catalog throws at load, and a run without a window simply has no budget

tools.name: three-stage-tool-dispatch-prepare-dispatch-finalize
tools.what: A Tool is a plain data+behaviour record (name/description/inputSchema plus OPTIONAL policy metadata: timeoutMs, isConcurrencySafe, isReadOnly, getArgv, exposure, searchHint) and the registry is the single enforcement point. prepare() is fail-closed at the approval seam (unknown tool throws, deny throws, 'ask' consults the optional guardian first and then the human answerer, and with NO answerer the call throws 'approval required but no answerer registered (fail closed)'); monotonic guards run UNCONDITIONALLY before dispatch so no decision can bypass them. Dispatch is the only overlapping stage (the tools/execute cascade around the real body); prepare/finalize stay in the ordered lane, and the per-dispatch decision is returned through the emit chain rather than a shared closure slot so concurrent prepares cannot race.
invariants: Decisions are a closed vocabulary merged monotonically allow < ask < deny; an out-of-vocabulary kind is a hard error, never allow
Monotonic guards are vetoes that no decision can outrank
Same-layer duplicate registration is a hard error; child scopes get their own registry and may shadow by name
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed by default; the one fail-open point is 'no decision at all normalizes to allow' (documented pre-M13 semantics)

tools.name: deferred-tool-exposure-with-search-driven-promotion
tools.what: Exposure is a three-value model on the tool ('hidden' never appears in schemas(); 'deferred' appears only after its name is returned by search(); everything else is 'direct') plus a registry-side promotion set that is one-way for the registry's lifetime and is removed together with the tool on unregister. The search engine is pluggable and its absence is loud: installSearch(fn) sets the hook and search() throws 'no search engine installed' until then, the corpus handed to the engine is deferredSearchIndex() (raw metadata of only the deferred tools), and every returned name is promoted for the NEXT provider call.
invariants: Promotion is one-way and survives across provider calls
A re-mount must not inherit stale promotions (unregister clears them)
tools.failurePolicy: fail-loud: search() without an engine throws; an empty corpus is never silently searched

constants.name: deferred corpus
constants.value: deferredSearchIndex(): raw metadata of deferred tools only (searchHint included when present)

tools.name: bm25-tool-retrieval-with-four-selection-modes
tools.what: A dependency-free BM25 engine (k1 1.2 / b 0.75, deterministic name tie-break) over a caller-supplied corpus, with strict precedence: an exact case-insensitive name match returns that single tool immediately; 'select:a,b' resolves EXACT names and throws on an unknown selector (and on more matches than the limit); '+term' tokens become REQUIRED (every one must be in the document's token set) while the remaining terms only rank; otherwise all terms rank. Document text is the name plus camelCase/dash/underscore split name plus description plus searchHint plus recursively harvested JSON-schema titles/descriptions/property names/enum values.
invariants: An agent that knows the name is never at the mercy of a ranker
A missing exact selector fails loud instead of returning a fuzzy list
tools.failurePolicy: fail-loud at validation boundaries (empty query, non-integer/out-of-range limit, unknown selector); zero matches is a normal empty array

tools.name: fs-tool-boundary-returned-failures-toctou-re-check-atomic-writes
tools.what: The five workspace file tools (read, edit, write, apply_patch, list_dir) RETURN expected filesystem failures as { error, code } instead of throwing (softFail converts an FsToolError or a whitelisted Node errno; anything else still throws), because a throwing tool body makes the agent discard the batch and append neither tool/result nor turn/end, so the call read to the model as 'hung'. edit is a guarded read-modify-write: uniqueness, binary/UTF-8 validity, an optional observedMtimeMs, and a re-stat snapshot comparison (assertSnapshotFresh) before the write close the read->write TOCTOU window; line endings are detected on a 4096-char sample, normalized to LF for matching, then restored. Writes are same-directory temp + atomic rename with mkdir -p and best-effort temp unlink.
invariants: Only whitelisted errno/typed failures are returned; a programming error still fails the turn
A relative input is confined to the workspace ('..' escape refused) but an ABSOLUTE input is taken as-is and may point outside the workspace
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft at the tool boundary, fail-closed on every safety check it can make (escape refusal, stale version, ambiguous edit, binary/UTF-8, add-onto-existing, malformed patch)

constants.name: SOFT_ERRNO set
constants.value: ENOENT, EACCES, EPERM, EISDIR, ENOTDIR, EEXIST, EMFILE, ENOSPC, EROFS, EBUSY

constants.name: atomic temp name
constants.value: .<basename>.<6 random bytes hex>.tmp in the target directory

tools.name: codex-style-structured-patch-application
tools.what: apply_patch is strict and fail-closed on its parser: it must start with '*** Begin Patch' and end with '*** End Patch', a duplicate path in one patch is an error, unknown lines are errors, content after End Patch is an error, '*** Move to:' is explicitly unsupported in v0 (use delete+add), and an Add File onto an existing path is refused before writing. Update hunks are applied with a forward-only cursor and reverse-order splicing, and the hunk loop STOPS at the first failing hunk, reporting applied-so-far plus the error so the model can recover.
invariants: A silently ignored directive or a partial multi-file patch must not leave an unexplained workspace state
Failure is reported with the partial progress, never rolled back silently
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed per hunk with an explicit applied/errors report

tools.name: structured-line-diff-with-work-budget-and-honest-windowing
tools.what: The diff algorithm is NOT hand-rolled (the `diff` library's structuredPatch does LCS/Myers); this package owns normalization, hunk splitting and rendering. Oversized inputs are WINDOWED with position-aligned head/tail pairs instead of truncating the diff: head compares rows [0..N) on both sides, the tail pair is compared only when the two absolute ranges OVERLAP, and the union range never re-diffs head rows — a window of one side is never diffed against a positionally skewed window of the other, because that would fabricate deletions/additions from the skew. A hard 750 ms abortable budget yields an honest bounded result (no hunks, truncated:true) instead of blocking the turn.
invariants: A fabricated change is a lying diff: a size delta must appear as surplus rows, not boundary skew
'\ No newline at end of file' annotates the previous row instead of consuming one
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft and bounded: no path throws for pathological input; oversized input and timeouts degrade to flagged truncated results

tools.name: shell-resolution-honesty-and-argv-view-for-policy
tools.what: resolveShell prefers bash when bash is on PATH and otherwise returns pwsh, but the bash TOOL hardcodes argv ['bash','-c',command] so a tool named bash can never silently execute PowerShell; when bash is unavailable the tool RETURNS a synthetic result (exitCode -1 with a legible stderr pointing at the pwsh tool) rather than an empty-output spawn failure. getArgv is a minimal in-package quote parser supplied as Tool.getArgv so the approval policy can classify a command from its argv without spawning, normalizing the bypass shapes the comment names (r\m, 'r''m', r""m).
invariants: A tool named bash never runs another shell
Retention is opt-in at the tool-return layer only; exec keeps the full stream
tools.failurePolicy: fail-open at the tool boundary for a missing shell (a synthetic result, not a throw); a refused sandbox is NOT handled here and propagates out of the tool body

tools.name: process-execution-service-confinement-tree-kill-spill-background-jobs
tools.what: exec spawns argv (optionally confined), kills whole process trees on timeout/abort, normalizes CRLF, captures stdout/stderr with an optional memory-tail + disk-spill collector, and owns a background-job registry with get/list/kill. Confinement is resolved ONCE at spawn from the command-carried policy: no policy or danger-full-access passes through, a confined policy with NO provider throws SandboxUnavailableError before spawning, and a confined policy with a provider runs assertSandboxCapable then provider.confine, keeping the ConfinedArgv (denialSignatures/runnerFailureRules/enforcement) on the handle for the done path. A runner failure (bwrap exit 125 etc.) is TRANSLATED into a SandboxUnavailableError rejection because the command body never executed. One killTree implementation serves the timeout timer, the returned kill() and the external abort listener, and an external abort is explicitly NOT a timeout (timedOut stays false).
invariants: A confined command must never run unconfined just because a backend is missing
Only the tool body overlaps; the committed result shape is never dropped
Spill is foreground-only: runBackground keeps plain stream accumulation into job.stdout
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed at the sandbox boundary (missing provider, capability mismatch, runner failure all become SandboxUnavailableError); everything else is ordinary result reporting

tools.name: pty-terminal-service-with-ring-buffered-re-readable-output
tools.what: A TerminalService owns node-pty sessions with a per-terminal chunk log addressed by UTF-16-code-unit offsets: read(offset) returns [offset, offset+maxBytes) and is repeatable (log-view semantics, not a consuming queue), and the internal ring drops the oldest chunks past RING_MAX. Ownership is enforced per PTY: open() records the caller's exec.sessionId as ownerSessionId and getOwned throws TERMINAL_OWNER_MISMATCH when the caller's session id differs (an unowned session stays accessible). Sizing is tracked service-side rather than read from node-pty, and pty.resize is issued only while running and after the ConPTY is ready, with a sync throw swallowed. Known win32 ConPTY agent noise on the error path is filtered and a report that is ONLY noise converts to a returned benign result.
invariants: Offsets earlier than the ring start are served from the ring start (a documented shortcoming: the dropped prefix is unrecoverable)
One session must not drive another session's interactive terminal
tools.failurePolicy: fail-loud with a noise-tolerant error path: unknown ids and owner mismatches throw, dispose rejects all pending exit waiters, PTY noise-only errors are downgraded to a benign returned result

tools.name: ripgrep-backed-search-tools-with-capped-deferred-result-sets
tools.what: glob and grep both shell out to a lazily resolved @vscode/ripgrep binary through the exec service (lazy because that package resolves its platform binary at module evaluation, so a static import would fail the whole loader on a partial install), run in the assembly workspace so relative paths resolve like every other fs tool, and expose themselves as DEFERRED tools with a searchHint. Result sets are capped (glob 100 sorted by mtime with VCS directories excluded twice, once as a directory and once as a subtree; grep 250 parsing rg --json lines and skipping malformed ones). Exit-code semantics are explicit: rg exit 1 with no matches is a normal empty result, any other non-zero exit is returned as { matches: [], error }.
invariants: A spawn failure must never look to the model like 'nothing matched'
Both tools are deferred, read-only and concurrency-safe
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft for execution failures (a caught error becomes { matches: [], error }) and fail-loud for caller errors (an empty pattern throws)

tools.name: filesystem-watch-as-baseline-filtered-deltas
tools.what: A chokidar-backed event stream exposed as an AsyncIterable of { path, kind: add|change|unlink } whose events are DELTAS against a baseline walked synchronously at create time: the watcher runs with ignoreInitial:false and filters echoes by consulting the baseline promise, which closes the create-before-scan race in which chokidar's ignoreInitial would swallow a write that happened right after creation. change/unlink are never filtered. The first read awaits chokidar readiness while early events buffer in a queue; a single error is latched and surfaces once per iterator (startup errors release readiness so the first read cannot hang; late errors reject a waiting next() and terminate the stream). WIRING: this package is an UNCONNECTED SEAM — it exports no tool surface and has no non-test caller anywhere in the repo (every import of createFsWatcher is in packages/fs-watch/test/watch.test.ts), so in every shipped host no filesystem watcher exists.
invariants: A late subscriber must not miss an early write, and a pre-existing file must not be reported as an addition
Ignore semantics are path-SEGMENT based (any depth, exact name match)
tools.failurePolicy: fail-soft/degrade-not-throw: an unreadable root during the baseline walk is skipped, events after close are dropped, and the only error channel is the latched pendingError

tools.name: backend-snapshot-rollback-engine-rewind
tools.what: A per-session RewindStore keeps a journal of points (points.jsonl, atomically rewritten) plus content-addressed pre-image blobs written only if missing; paths are workspace-relative keys through one seam that refuses absolute paths, '..' segments and empty results; meta.json binds the journal to the absolute workspace and every service surface plus every journal-writing path fails closed with REWIND_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH on a foreign journal. Undo semantics are 'rewind to the END of turn T-1' with lazy conflict classification: each record stores the preBlob, isNewFile and the afterHash re-read at finalize, plan() compares the current disk hash against afterHash to classify clean vs modified/deleted/created, and conflicts are STILL executed (a rewind is destructive by design, honestly marked). Crash leftovers (a pending.json whose turn has no point) are archived into orphaned.jsonl and REPORTED through plan().orphanedTurns, never fabricated into a point and never auto-restored. The git probe is read-only evidence (rev-parse, status --porcelain=v1 -z, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0), memoized, fail-soft to [] and never turned into file operations.
invariants: Identical files addressed differently must not alias twice
A capture failure must never change tool behavior (paths outside the workspace are captured as UNTRACKED)
A file-op error during execute prevents the journal truncate so retry data survives
tools.failurePolicy: fail-closed for safety/exclusivity (workspace mismatch, path refusal, invalid target turn, corrupt journal) and fail-open for evidence (the git probe never throws)

tools.name: durable-workspace-registry-with-a-bounded-file-walker
tools.what: A Workspace registry over the coordinator's generic document store owns exactly one versioned whole-state document and NO filesystem: create() does pure string normalization and the caller (host route) realpaths and stats the directory before calling, so the path-trust decision stays in the layer that owns the route. Every operation — mutations AND reads — goes through one serialization chain so two concurrent read-modify-write cycles cannot interleave and a list during a mutation observes either the pre- or post-state. Archive is a DISPLAY layer over accounting: archivedSessionIds is registry-GLOBAL, archiving KEEPS the session's slot, is idempotent and rejects an UNKNOWN id fail-loud against coordinator.list() so a typo cannot record a dangling id. The separate walker is bounded and deterministic (caps, early frontier abandonment, exact-name skips, symlinks never followed, codepoint sort, case-insensitive substring matching with NO ranking).
invariants: The registry computes no absolute path, stats nothing and never creates/deletes a directory
The walk never follows symlinks, so a link cannot drag it outside the workspace or loop
tools.failurePolicy: fail-loud on its own invariants (blank path, blank title, unknown workspace, duplicate title, unknown session on archive, corrupt document) and fail-soft only below the walk root (an unreadable NESTED directory is skipped; an unreadable ROOT rethrows because an empty answer would be a silent lie)

tools.name: external-content-tool-surface
tools.what: The network/retrieval tool surface: webfetch fetches (redirect-following, http/https only, caller abort signal forwarded, user-agent i-harness/0.1), size-caps the BODY read, strips HTML to text, detects the title and head-tail caps the rendered text with a truncation note. websearch is registered ONLY when an id-keyed websearch provider is usable, so with no provider the tool is simply ABSENT from the catalog rather than present-and-failing - a fail-closed tool-absence posture the provider seam also enforces by throwing NO_PROVIDER on a pinned-but-missing id and MULTIPLE_PROVIDERS when more than one is registered without a pin. Every result carries EXTERNAL_WEB_CONTENT_NOTICE as a distinct envelope FIELD (never concatenated into content/sources), so the trust boundary stays structured data the model can be told about rather than a polluted text stream. Both tools are read-only, concurrency-safe and declare a 30 s timeoutMs, so the tool timeout guard actually bounds them.
invariants: The external-content notice must stay a separate envelope field, never concatenated into content or sources text (packages/web/src/index.ts:6-13)
websearch must be ABSENT rather than failing at call time when no provider is usable - "no built-in provider is EVER registered" (packages/web/src/index.ts:85-91)
Only http/https URLs are accepted; any other protocol is refused before the fetch (packages/web/src/index.ts:60-62)
tools.failurePolicy: mixed: fail-closed on tool availability (no usable provider means the websearch tool is never registered, and a pinned-missing provider throws NO_PROVIDER synchronously) and fail-loud at call time for protocol and fetch failures (WEB_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL / WEB_FETCH_FAILED), while oversized bodies and oversized text degrade to a marked truncation rather than an error

subagent.name: durable-delegated-task-protocol-with-identity-cas
subagent.what: Delegated work is tracked by a durable task record with a status state machine accepted -> running -> {completed | error | cancelled | recovery-required}, keyed by a three-part identity (parentSessionId + callEventSeq, else toolCallId, else a fresh anon key) and persisted as one coordinator document `task-<stateId>`. submit() records 'accepted' immediately (an exact retry ADOPTS the existing record; a mismatched retry throws TaskIdentityConflictError); claim() is the only accepted->running edge and is called in spawn_agent AFTER spawnChild returns, i.e. after the child's initial run has already started — so 'running' is a recorded observation, not an admission gate. Terminalization is CAS (a record with an outcome is never re-settled) and enqueues a parent-notification row. The doc key uses a dash, not a colon, because a colon makes an NTFS alternate data stream that breaks rename.
invariants: The real admission gates are the identity key plus the concurrency/depth quotas — NOT the 'running' status
A terminal record is never re-settled
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed on quota and identity (TaskConcurrencyLimitError / TaskIdentityConflictError) and on unknown ids; persistence is report-never-reject at the document layer so the in-memory registry stays authoritative for the run

subagent.name: durable-notification-outbox-with-injectable-admission
subagent.what: Parent notification is a durable outbox: each row is pending|delivered|woken|error|suppressed, drain() re-checks each row's CURRENT status (idempotent, no double-admit), SUPPRESSES delivery when the parent chain was cancelled, and calls the injected admit() seam with an XML-ish <task> framing (task_result / task_error). A failed admit records 'error' and the row is retried on the next drain. With no admit seam, drain returns 0 and nothing is lost — delivery is then durable-only.
invariants: Delivery is never duplicated across drains (status re-check)
A cancelled parent chain suppresses rather than drops-without-trace
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-soft but durable: a failed delivery is recorded and retried, never silently dropped

subagent.name: crash-recovery-by-classification-never-re-dispatch
subagent.what: On restore, ambiguous in-flight attempts are classified from the DURABLE child log rather than re-run: classifyRestoredTasks loads each unfinished task's child session after the seed length and looks for turn/end plus the last assistant/message — turn/end present becomes completed with that text, a missing log becomes 'dispatch-unknown', and a log without turn/end becomes 'response-interrupted'. Everything else in restore maps running->error ('interrupted by resume') while 'waiting' is preserved so a queued followup can be re-driven, and the parent session log additionally gets a replayed terminal job/status so a log-only fold agrees with the document.
invariants: An ambiguous in-flight attempt is never re-dispatched
A queued followup survives a resume
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-visible: an unresolvable child log becomes recovery-required / 'child log unavailable after resume' rather than a silent empty stub

subagent.name: concurrency-and-depth-quotas
subagent.what: Two independent quotas govern delegation: a CONCURRENCY quota over non-terminal accepted+running records (submit throws TaskConcurrencyLimitError when runningCount() >= maxConcurrency, default Infinity so a host must opt in) and a DEPTH quota read from the caller session header's delegationDepth (default 1, so a top-level caller may spawn but a subagent may not nest). The code documents a carried depth-binding limitation: the tool mount is shared and binds ONE root parent session, so every caller resolves depth from the root and a host-raised maxDepth > 1 would under-enforce — moot in the shipped surface because no builtin role carries spawn_agent.
invariants: Both quotas fail closed at the submit boundary
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed: TaskConcurrencyLimitError on the concurrency quota

subagent.name: team-scope-event-sourced-roster-task-board-and-mailbox
subagent.what: A Team is a lead plus named durable teammates over the SAME subagent machinery, event-sourced on the lead session's log with exactly four validated team/* events (team/member, team/task, team/message/queued, team/message/delivered) under strict schema validation with immutable member identity and +1 task revisions; foldTeam is a full replay that skips non-team events and recovers the canonical teamId from the FIRST team/* event. Every mutation goes through a serialized transaction whose callback is PURE-READ — it runs against a CLONE, candidates are validated in order, then applied to the live state, appended and flushed, so 'invalid never enters state or log' holds by construction. Delivery is durability-before-ack: a message counts delivered only after the target's session log is FLUSHED, so a flush failure leaves it queued for recoverRoot. Competing team tools REPLACE the same-named subagent tools on the shared parent registry and unmount restores them, making unmount a true reverse of mount; Lead-only authority (spawn_teammate, interrupt_agent) is enforced at the DOMAIN layer, and write scopes are advisory (overlap warns, never blocks).
invariants: Events are applied and appended BEFORE flush (at-least-once); onCommit fires only after flush resolves
One team per run (module-level reservation)
Write-scope overlap is advice, not enforcement
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed: config validation runs before any side effect, provisioning fails closed when a child session cannot PROVE durability, and delivery returns false on a flush rejection

subagent.name: static-yaml-workflow-runs-as-one-background-job
subagent.what: Workflows are static YAML files under <workspace>/workflow/*.yml; one run executes as ONE background job (id workflow-<n>) in a workflow-owned store that deliberately mirrors ExecService's job contract including the exact `unknown job: <id>` error string, because that store is the THIRD layer of subagent's job_* fallback chain. Steps run strictly sequentially with no DAG/parallel/conditions/loops (deliberately not implemented); on_failure:continue keeps the loop going but does NOT launder the failure — the run still ends 'error' with the first failing exit code, while 'stop' skips the remaining steps. Parameter interpolation is plain string substitution before spawn with the same trust level as the bash tool (only DECLARED params interpolate; unknown ${...} stays verbatim) and a missing required param fails loud BEFORE any job is created.
invariants: A run never reports partial success
Params are model-authored command text, so no escaping is attempted
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-loud then fail-visible: a schema/YAML violation throws WorkflowParseError, the registry catches per file and warns+skips, and any failing step marks the run 'error'

subagent.name: durable-reminders-whose-state-is-the-event-log
subagent.what: Per-session reminders are `schedule/change` v1 events with create/delete/dispatch operations folded last-wins per id, and a dispatch event acts as the durable ACCEPTANCE record: the driver appends the dispatch BEFORE delivering, so a delivery without a durable accept is impossible and a restart re-drives exactly the still-overdue remainder. Three rule kinds (after / at / every) with `every` advancing by a generation-anchored occurrence without enumerating a backlog. Reminder text is framed injection-resistant: dynamic fields are JSON-escaped and the model is explicitly told the prompt is untrusted reminder content. Creation validation is strict with machine-coded ScheduleInputError (non-empty prompt, strictly-future target, canonical four-digit-year UTC instants, and a frequency floor so a model cannot create a hot reminder loop).
invariants: Durable accept precedes delivery
Schedule state has no separate store: the session event stream IS the state
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed on delivery (append failure means no delivery, recorded in deliveryErrors) and fail-visible on corruption (a corrupt session stream is skipped for the tick with a warning)

subagent.name: whole-list-todo-snapshot
subagent.what: todo_write is a whole-list snapshot model: the model must send the WHOLE list every call and it REPLACES the previous one, which keeps status tracking race-free (last write wins, no merge logic), and the list lives in the session log as todo/write events so projection is a pure function and persistence mirrors it for free. Validation is fail-loud inside the tool body: empty/whitespace content and duplicate content throw, and more than one in_progress item throws unless allowParallelInProgress is set. The tool declares isConcurrencySafe:true (a whole-list replace has no read-modify-write hazard) while isReadOnly is false.
invariants: One in_progress item is the planner invariant by default
The projection is a pure last-event-wins fold so replay is deterministic
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-loud: validation errors throw out of the tool body (unlike the fs family) and there is no try/catch in the module

subagent.name: plan-mode-as-log-state
subagent.what: Plan mode is log state, not process state: entering appends { plan/mode, mode:'on', proposal } AND the proposal as a regular user/message (so the model sees the plan request), and the projection is latest-wins via derivePlanMode. Exit is SOFT and idempotent — exitPlanMode returns false when plan mode is not active instead of throwing, and the tool reports { active: exitPlanMode(session) }. The exit_plan_mode tool is mounted idempotently by name (ensurePlanModeTool checks tools.get first) and can be withdrawn by name.
invariants: Attribution (the proposal) stays on the marker while the model-visible text stays a normal user turn
Calling exit twice, or when never in plan mode, is not an error
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-soft: no throw anywhere except the underlying append validation; the tool is mounted by the assembly but never withdrawn there (withdrawPlanModeTool has no in-tree caller)

subagent.name: whole-snapshot-goal-domain-with-mandatory-cas
subagent.what: Every non-clear goal mutation carries the COMPLETE post-change goal (id, revision, objective, phase, optional maxGoalRounds) so the projection is a pure last-wins replay with no separate state store, while a clear carries only a tombstone ref and projects to null. Mutations are PURE planners: applyGoalMutation never mutates its input and never appends — it returns { event, next } and the caller owns the log. CAS is mandatory: every mutation needs a ref matching the current id AND revision, else GoalStateError('goal-stale-ref'), and typed codes (goal-invalid / goal-exists / goal-none / goal-stale-ref / goal-invalid-transition) are the host contract with the HTTP status mapping owned by the route. Validation is asymmetric like the rest of the engine: strict writes, forgiving reads (a malformed persisted goal/change leaves the projection unchanged rather than throwing).
invariants: The event IS the change: replay alone rebuilds the state, so a snapshot cannot drift from a log of deltas
Revision is bumped on every change and is the only concurrency control
subagent.failurePolicy: fail-closed for mutations (every invalid request throws a typed GoalStateError) and fail-safe for projection (malformed events are skipped)

subagent.name: jobs-as-a-two-source-projection
subagent.what: The jobs surface is a PURE projection with two independent data sources producing ONE shape: the durable subagent snapshot document is the initial snapshot (GET /api/sessions/:id/jobs) and a fold of `job/status` session events (last-wins by jobId, whole-job snapshot per event) is the realtime update over the existing mux session stream — no new endpoint. The durable doc shape is INLINED STRUCTURALLY on purpose so web-host never depends on the subagent runtime; if the producer's shape drifts, the route's mapping warns loudly rather than silently mis-serving, and a foreign/corrupt doc maps to an empty list. The kill vocabulary ('cancellation-requested' | 'already-finished') is the live registry's own strings, and an unknown job is an honest 409 rather than a silent 200.
invariants: A projection owns no store and invents no fields
The realtime path adds no endpoint (it reuses the mux session stream)
subagent.failurePolicy: honest degradation rather than fail-open/closed: a foreign/corrupt doc becomes an empty list with a loud warn at the route; an unknown kill target raises JobKillUnknownJobError so the transport answers 409

safety.name: startup-applied-os-sandbox-that-refuses-to-run-unprotected
safety.what: The sandbox seam's contract is that confine() must return enforcing argv or THROW — silent unconfined passthrough is forbidden. exec resolves confinement once at spawn: a confined policy with no provider throws SandboxUnavailableError BEFORE spawning, a capability mismatch throws, and a provider whose runner failed to start (bwrap exit 125 / windows-acl-run exit 127, matched by signature) is translated into SandboxUnavailableError rather than surfaced as an ordinary non-zero exit, because the command body never executed. sandbox-local dispatches on process.platform with three fail-closed arms (win32 without an injected ACL backend, linux without a successful bwrap probe, any other platform) and every arm either confines or throws; no passthrough arm exists. The Linux probe runs a REAL confined 'true' rather than 'bwrap --version' because --version passes on hosts where user namespaces are blocked.
invariants: A policy demanding read isolation on a backend that cannot declare it is REFUSED, never degraded
Both local backends declare capabilities { readIsolation: false } honestly
A confined command never runs unconfined just because a backend is missing
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed: SandboxUnavailableError carries the message '...refusing to run the command unconfined', SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE is the stable code string, and the escalation approval path throws when no approval channel is composed

safety.name: confinement-covers-only-shell-fs-fs-search-and-terminal-have-no-sandbox-integration
safety.what: Only the shell tools carry a sandbox policy: ShellToolDeps has an optional sandboxPolicy that is attached to both exec.run and exec.runBackground as the `sandbox` field, and the provider is handed to registerExec which composes the exec service. Everything else is unconfined. packages/fs/src contains ZERO sandbox symbols and FsToolDeps carries only workspace + rewind; the fs 'confinement' is resolvePath's relative-path '..' refusal, while an ABSOLUTE path is taken as-is and may point outside the workspace. fs-search has no sandbox field and calls exec.run with only { argv, cwd }, so ripgrep runs unconfined even under a read-only session mode. terminal has no sandbox parameter on its PTY tools (TerminalToolDeps carries only service + cwd) and no timeoutMs on any terminal_*/process_* tool. The practical consequence of the shell-only wiring: a sandbox refusal inside a shell tool is not caught, so it propagates out of the tool body and the agent records tool/error and discards the whole batch — one refused command fails the entire turn; the background variant instead becomes an errored job.
invariants: Write-path confinement for the fs family is a path check, not OS-level isolation
'A win-ACL sandbox exists' does not imply 'every file operation is confined'
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed at the shell boundary but with turn-wide cost (the refusal kills the turn rather than degrading); fs/fs-search/terminal have no refusal path at all because they have no policy input

safety.name: read-isolation-is-declared-but-absent-the-gate-is-never-armed-outside-tests
safety.what: No backend declares read isolation. Both local backends declare capabilities { readIsolation: false }; the Linux bwrap profile uses `--ro-bind / /`, so the whole filesystem stays READABLE (writes are isolated, content is not); and the Windows ACL backend's own header states that writes are restricted while reads, network and process visibility are NOT, because WRITE_RESTRICTED intersects only write accesses. The only related mechanism is a refusal gate: assertSandboxCapable throws SandboxUnavailableError when policy.requireReadIsolation === true and the provider does not declare readIsolation:true, and a missing declaration is treated as { readIsolation: false }. Repo-wide, requireReadIsolation is set ONLY by tests (packages/sandbox/test/enforcement.test.ts and packages/exec/test/enforcement.test.ts) and by no src caller, so in composed use the gate is never armed; the in-code comment itself records that every provider is readIsolation:false and the gate is a contract left for future account-style backends.
invariants: Capabilities unknown means NOT read-isolated (fail closed, never fail open)
A demand for read isolation is an opt-in that turns capability absence into a refuse-to-run
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed by contract, inert in practice: the refusal path exists and is unit-tested but no shipped composition can reach it because nothing sets requireReadIsolation

safety.name: windows-write-restricted-token-backend
safety.what: The Windows backend builds a WRITE_RESTRICTED token whose restricting-SID list is mode-selected: read-only gets [logon SID, EVERYONE] and workspace-write adds the per-workspace write SID plus an optional per-temp write SID; Authenticated Users and INTERACTIVE/LOCAL are deliberately absent from BOTH lists (AU fails the WMI namespace check and standing AU ACEs on the C: root close a tree-creation escape; INTERACTIVE/LOCAL is dropped because the Public tree grants writes to INTERACTIVE). Because read-only carries no write SID, a stale workspace ACE stays inert. Capability identity is split: a deterministic per-workspace SID derived from the canonical workspace path and a domain-separated per-private-temp SID. Grant lifecycle is asymmetric — workspace ACEs are STANDING (the cross-session reuse cache) while temp ACEs are REVOCABLE and removed by dispose() — and grants are idempotent: grantWrite reads the directory's explicit DACL and SKIPS the apply when the exact ACE is already present, under a per-path exclusive LockFileEx lock. Confinement prefixes an argv runner that spawns the child under that token (never unrestricted) and assigns the suspended child to a kill-on-close job before it runs.
invariants: The per-call SandboxPolicy is the enforcement input; the construction options' `mode` is never read by the factory
Every Win32 call is checked; the confined child is never spawned unrestricted; a runner failure exits 127 with a matchable signature
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed at every level: construction throws on a missing/non-directory writableDir, a grant failure cleans up and rethrows, init() rolls back revocable grants/SIDs/handles before rethrowing, confine() after dispose throws SandboxUnavailableError, dispose() reports every cleanup failure as AggregateError

safety.name: sandbox-escalation-ladder-declared-tested-no-production-caller
safety.what: A strictly-wider escalation ladder exists in the seam: WIDER_MODES maps read-only -> [workspace-write, danger-full-access] and workspace-write -> [danger-full-access]; approveEscalation rejects a non-wider target, a missing approver and a missing agent, and maps outcome rejected/cancelled/unavailable to distinct errors; sandboxDenialMarker and escalationHintMarker render tool-output TEXT markers (not SessionEvents) and validateEscalationArgs checks the advertised argument shape. Repo-wide the entire surface appears in production src only at its definition and re-export — the only other references are the package's own tests — and NO tool schema declares the `sandbox_permissions` / `justification` parameters that the marker text advertises, so the ladder does not exist on any production path. writableRoots() and canonicalPath() are likewise test-only in composed use; writableRoots is nonetheless the single home of the workspace-write meaning (workspaceRoot + /tmp + tmpdir(), canonicalized and deduped) so the profile dialects and any in-process fence cannot drift apart.
invariants: Escalation is strictly-wider and checked at execution time, never baked into a tool schema
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed: approveEscalation throws when no approval service/channel is composed; but the whole path is unreachable in production

constants.name: writableRoots (workspace-write)
constants.value: workspaceRoot + '/tmp' + tmpdir(), canonicalized and deduped; read-only => []

safety.name: sandbox-mode-resolution-and-advisory-prompt-text
safety.what: The effective sandbox mode for a session is resolved request.mode > the session's LAST sandbox/mode event (the scan runs backwards, last-writer-wins) > the configured default ('read-only'), then path.resolve on the workspace root. The rendered policy text is injected into the system prompt and is explicitly ADVISORY: it tells the model not to refuse a required modification from the policy alone but to try an available tool normally and follow any denial/escalation guidance it returns. The resolved policy object is passed to BOTH the enforcer and this renderer so they cannot drift.
invariants: A mode change is a log append; there is no separate mutable mode field
The same resolved policy feeds enforcement and the prompt text
safety.failurePolicy: no enforcement here (pure resolution): an unrecognized mode falls through to the default arm and renders an empty string

safety.name: three-layer-approval-policy-with-an-advisory-danger-classifier
safety.what: The approval policy has three layers as implemented: a readOnly tool is allowed; a `write` with no path or a path outside the workspace asks; any other non-readOnly tool asks (layer-1 fallback); EXCEPT bash/pwsh, which ask ONLY when classifyDanger() != 'none' — a benign registered shell command therefore executes with NO approval even with askForNonReadOnly true and no answerer. For the shell tools the safety boundary IS the classifier, and it is advisory: it parses the tool's own getArgv output, and the file records the bypass surface it is meant to survive (quoted 'r''m', metachar '; rm -rf /', and control flow whose every basename is harmless). Deny-on-metachar treats any argv token containing one of 7 metachars (the array is [";", "&&", "|", "$(", "`", ">", "<"]; a '>>' token is caught by the ">" membership test rather than being a separate element) as dangerous even when every basename looks harmless, and a force-delete is 'extreme' only when its targets lie outside the workspace or name a top-level system path. approvalPolicy 'never' promotes an ask-decision into deny-with-reason instead of consulting the answerer, and the policy seeds BOTH a plain listener and a waterfall handler from one shared decide() because a waterfall-only handler is invisible to ctx.resolveDecision.
invariants: Over-asking is the intended direction at the metachar layer: it is deliberately deny-on-metachar, not a precise effect model
A returned decision object must not be able to short-circuit an ancestor guard (the handler returns undefined rather than {kind:'allow'})
safety.failurePolicy: mixed and explicitly tiered: an unknown tool asks (fail closed); 'no applicable decision' is undefined = allow, which for a benign shell command is deliberate fail-open; 'never' turns every ask into deny

safety.name: guardian-auto-review-subagent-with-fail-closed-verdict-and-breaker
safety.what: An optional LLM approval guardian spawns a dedicated no-tools 'reviewer' role via spawnChild with forkTurns 'none' (reclaimed in finally) and requires a strict-JSON verdict; only 'allow' falls through to the human answerer, while deny, timeout and malformed all DENY. Deny, timeout and malformed are all counted by a circuit breaker over the last 10 reviews at 3 non-allow outcomes, and the breaker has a durable mirror whose read failure yields a fresh CLOSED breaker (fail-soft on persistence). The reviewer's context is bounded (transcript maxChars 4000 / maxEvents 12, per-line slice 200).
invariants: A timeout or malformed verdict is treated as the stuck-reviewer failure the breaker exists for, not as model disagreement
Only an explicit allow reaches the human
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed deny on open breaker, timeout (cause:'timeout'), malformed JSON (cause:'malformed'), a missing reviewer entry and missing final text; the durable breaker mirror is fail-soft

safety.name: hooks-as-fail-closed-gates-and-fail-visible-observers
safety.what: User-configured hook handlers are spawned as subprocesses (no shell) with the HookContext as one JSON object on stdin, must emit exactly one JSON HookOutput object on stdout, are killed after timeoutMs and have stdout/stderr capped. The event list is exactly 9 events and each is classified as GATE or OBSERVER: pre-tool/post-tool, prompt/submit, stop and permission are gates (deny/ask, block:true, continue:false, a handler error, a non-zero exit, a timeout, unparseable stdout and a trust mismatch ALL become HookBlockedError), while session/start, session/end, subagent/stop and notification are observers where a trust failure or handler error is reported and skipped. Handler type (command | mcpTool | prompt | agent) only TAGS a handler for trust/audit in v1 — every handler is executed as `command.cmd args`. Per-run hash trust is a security boundary: the executed artifact's sha256 is recomputed on EVERY invocation and compared with the configured value. Config loading is strict about shape but distinguishes an EXPLICIT configPath (missing -> HookConfigError) from the default path (missing -> zero handlers). WIRING: createHookRegistry has ZERO non-test callers (every call site is packages/hooks/test/hooks.test.ts), so although the gate/observer semantics, the per-invocation trust hashing and the output validation are fully implemented and unit-tested, no shipped host mounts them: the only shipped consumer of this package is the TUI's read-only inventory panel (packages/tui/src/app/slash/impl/eco.ts:17 imports resolveHooksConfigPath/loadHooksConfig/HOOK_EVENTS, used at :72-85, rendered by packages/tui/src/views/light-hooks.ts:5). The gate layer is therefore an unconnected seam, not an active safety control.
invariants: A gate fails closed on every failure class; an observer never becomes fatal
ask is not wired to a question seam on main, so a permission 'ask' is a fail-closed DENY in v1
safety.failurePolicy: fail-closed for gates, fail-open-but-visible for observers

constants.name: HOOK_EVENTS
constants.value: 9: session/start, session/end, prompt/submit, pre-tool, post-tool, permission, stop, subagent/stop, notification

safety.name: agent-preset-as-scoped-per-agent-configuration
safety.what: A preset is a validated JSON shape (name/systemPrompt/tools/model) whose tools are resolved EVERY one BEFORE any scope mutation, so an unknown tool throws with no partial mount, and the resolved tools plus a 'preset' service go into a freshly mounted CHILD scope (lazily creating a tools/registry when the caller exposed none) so a preset cannot leak its tools or prompt into the parent. The I-harness-owned DEFAULT_AGENT_PRESET system prompt is the readable in-repo source and is treated as a BASE by the assembly — the assembly composes its runtime sections AFTER it and appends the sandbox policy context, while the user message always outranks the system prompt.
invariants: Resolution happens before any scope mutation (no half-mounted child)
The default prompt is a base, not the final prompt
safety.failurePolicy: fail-loud: parsePreset throws on a missing name/systemPrompt/tools and mountPreset throws on an unknown tool before any scope mutation

safety.name: repeat-call-nudge-guard-observational-never-blocking
safety.what: Counts consecutive identical tool calls by the key name + JSON.stringify(args) per Session (state in a WeakMap keyed by the Session object, so entries are GC'd with their session) and, at each configured threshold in a LIST (default [3,5,8]), appends an internal user/message nudge telling the model to consider changing approach. Any different key resets the counter to 1. Misconfiguration fails loud at construction (thresholds must be a non-empty array of integers >= 2).
invariants: Only an unbroken run of identical calls counts as a loop
The nudge is an internal message (internal:true, plugin source), not a user turn
safety.failurePolicy: observational — no deny or escalation path; only a message append

safety.name: tool-timeout-guard-converting-a-hang-into-tool-timeout
safety.what: A cascade handler on tools/execute enforces the TOOL's declared timeoutMs by swapping in a linked AbortController and, when its OWN timer fired, substituting {error, code:'TOOL_TIMEOUT'} at the TOP level of the raw value (spreading the tool's other fields) so it reads at tool/result.output.code. The guard's own timeout is distinguished from an upstream (parent) cancel by a local timedOut flag; the derived controller is linked to the upstream signal and unlinked in finally, and a tool that honors the abort by REJECTING still surfaces TOOL_TIMEOUT instead of propagating the rejection. The guard holds NO default: with no timeoutMs the call is unbounded, and the config object is an empty placeholder reserved for future knobs.
invariants: Per-tool policy stays with the tool; the guard has no hardcoded tunables
A parent cancel is not a timeout
safety.failurePolicy: converts a hang into a structured failure value rather than a throw

safety.name: tool-retry-guard-with-re-entrancy-protection
safety.what: A cascade handler re-dispatches a tool call whose result carries TOOL_TIMEOUT, with exponential backoff + jitter and a retry cap. Mount order is load-bearing: this guard must be registered BEFORE the timeout guard so it stays OUTER and sees the raw TOOL_TIMEOUT, and the ORIGINAL caller signal is captured before the inner timeout guard swaps exec.abortSignal (after a TOOL_TIMEOUT that controller is aborted, so reading the signal later would falsely stop retrying). Re-dispatch deliberately bypasses the registry's pre-execute hooks, the monotonic guards and post-execute — approval was already granted — and marks the frame with markCascadeRedispatch so once-per-logical-call cascade handlers (hooks pre/post-tool) skip their own run. A WeakSet of in-flight dispatch objects guards re-entrancy: a nested frame delegates to next() instead of retrying, because re-invoking the cascade would otherwise multiply attempts exponentially.
invariants: Only TOOL_TIMEOUT triggers a retry
A retry frame is not a new logical call (the redispatch marker)
safety.failurePolicy: bounded best-effort recovery: after maxRetries the last timeout result is returned unchanged; an upstream abort during backoff stops retrying

model.name: provider-agnostic-model-seam-with-retry-only-before-output
model.what: One uniform six-level effort vocabulary ('off'|'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'|'max') where undefined means SEND NOTHING and an unsupported value is passed through VERBATIM so the provider's 400 surfaces — adapters never guess, clamp or special-case. The retrying client retries only when the error is retryable AND nothing has been produced yet AND a budget remains, because a restarted stream after output would duplicate text/reasoning/tool_call; budget exhaustion is ALWAYS a hard failure and retries are silent (no event seam). Error classification prefers a structured err.code found by walking the cause chain (depth 5) and only then falls back to message regexes; transport failures are re-described with a proxy/CA remediation hint and a caller abort is named as an abort, and the text never includes headers or the API key. assertMessagesFromLog pins the model-visible array to deriveMessages(session) by JSON equality, and images are never silently dropped for text-only routes: part-level images become a deterministic placeholder carrying the first 8 base64 chars and canonical dataBase64 occurrences in tool-role STRING content are masked.
invariants: Never default any provider: an unsupported effort reaches the provider
Model-visible messages must derive from the session log (audit F01-3)
Images on a text-only route are replaced by a labelled placeholder, never silently dropped
model.failurePolicy: fail-loud with bounded retry: exhaustion throws the underlying failure whichever style the provider used; invalid policy config throws at resolve time

constants.name: DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_CODES
constants.value: ['RATE_LIMIT','SERVER','TIMEOUT','TRANSPORT','EMPTY_RESPONSE'] (CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED and QUOTA are classified but NOT in the default retry set)

model.name: five-wire-adapters-with-per-generation-reasoning-translation
model.what: Five protocol adapters implement the same seam: Anthropic Messages (SSE from /v1/messages), OpenAI Responses, OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, Gemini generateContent and AWS Bedrock Converse (through the AWS SDK). Reasoning translation is per-generation and deliberately fail-loud: Anthropic selects between an adaptive protocol (claude 4.6+ thinking:{type:'adaptive'} + output_config:{effort}, effort sent verbatim) and a legacy budget table (low 2048 / medium 8192 / high 16384) where an unmapped level falls through verbatim into budget_tokens; Gemini uses thinkingBudget for 2.5 and thinkingLevel for 3-and-unknown; Bedrock is family-keyed with the legacy shape as the unknown-family fallback so a rejecting model surfaces its 400. Shared wire discipline: configured headers merge UNDER the adapter's own headers with a case-insensitive collision drop (Fetch would comma-join Authorization and authorization into one corrupt value), a folded assistant step emits its text block BEFORE its tool_use/function_call blocks, and a tool result carrying images is split into a text tool-result plus a following user/synthetic message carrying the images. Errors are terminal {type:'error'} events with NO 'end' after them.
invariants: A request-level reasoningEffort outranks static config (spread order)
The model id for llm-openai comes from the adapter config, not LLMRequest.model
No usage/token event exists in the stream vocabulary — a recorded missing seam slot
model.failurePolicy: fail-loud/terminal: transport, non-OK HTTP, malformed tool arguments and a missing body all become terminal error events; llm-bedrock additionally propagates an SDK send rejection as an exception

model.name: scripted-mock-model-client-test-seam
model.what: A scripted ModelClient where each stream() call replays exactly ONE MockStep (its tool calls first, then its text, then 'end'), consuming the script destructively one step per model turn, so a script maps 1:1 to model turns and tests can assert a deterministic event sequence.
