Exhaustion is fail-loud: an empty script yields {type:'error'} 'mock script exhausted' instead of a silent end. It is reachable only when a caller explicitly opts into modelPolicy 'test-mock'.
invariants: A test double is never reachable by omission in production

model.name: provider-registry-model-discovery-probe-and-adapter-dispatch
model.what: The provider registry IS the directory: describeDirectory() is a view over profiles registered through register(), and runtime credentials never surface in a DirectoryEntry. Model discovery is a route-keyed probe chain (explicit registerProbe > an explicit modelsURL/baseURL with a generic built-in probe > the built-in openai-compatible probe > the profile's static models list > ProbeUnavailableError) with protocol-aware auth (anthropic-messages -> x-api-key + anthropic-version, gemini -> x-goog-api-key, else Bearer) where an ABSENT key omits the header entirely and a 10 s AbortSignal.timeout bounds every candidate. Response normalization accepts several vendor shapes with per-field capacity rules where the limit.{context,output} pair is ATOMIC (a half-pair drops both). buildModelClient dispatches on profile.protocol, wraps the client with the retrying client only when profile.retryPolicy is set, and an unknown protocol throws at build time. Websearch is a zero-default id-keyed seam (pin > exactly-one > error) with no built-in provider.
invariants: Never 'Bearer undefined': an absent key means no auth header at all
The registry is the only registration mechanism; the directory carries no secrets
model.failurePolicy: fail-loud / fail-closed: duplicate route registration throws, registration validates contextWindow and the retry policy, an unknown protocol throws at build, probe failures carry branded codes, and a malformed model row throws at load

model.name: typed-model-resolution-with-a-settings-backed-provider-runtime
model.what: The provider runtime merges registry templates with user settings rows into a directory view and resolves a session's model into a ready ModelClient binding or a TYPED unconfigured/invalid state. Precedence is explicit override 'provider:model' > session selection (provider + model + reasoningEffort) > settings llm.defaultModel, and resolveModel validates in order: provider existence, catalog membership, effort vocabulary, auth presence, auth resolution, ambient restriction, credential value, then buildClient — each failure a typed state with a reason rather than a throw. Auth is ref-based and derived from the view (apiKeyEnv -> {kind:'api-key-ref', ref}, bedrock -> {kind:'ambient'}, otherwise undefined), the runtime profile REPLACES the template's inline apiKey with the resolved value so a static template key cannot leak past the credential path, view precedence is user > template per field with a header MAP replacing the template's whole map, discovery caches per provider and merges probe rows UNDER manual rows (and is refused entirely for bedrock), and the api key ref name is generated from the provider id as <UPPER_SNAKE_ID>_API_KEY.
invariants: A binding is returned only after buildClient succeeds, so an unknown provider/model is never silently substituted
Settings never hold key material, only a ref name
model.failurePolicy: mixed by operation: read/resolve paths return typed states instead of throwing (including a caught auth-resolution failure) while mutations and discovery throw ('provider id is required', 'provider "<id>" is not configured', 'No API key configured for provider', bedrock manual-only)

constants.name: REASONING_EFFORTS
constants.value: { off, low, medium, high, xhigh, max }

constants.name: binding label
constants.value: '<displayName> · <modelId>' unless displayName is empty or equals the id, then '<providerId>:<modelId>'

model.name: ref-based-credential-store-with-env-over-file-precedence
model.what: One JSON document of ref -> value under the config home, with the rule 'refs not values': the settings document may hold only a ref NAME (apiKeyEnv), describe() is a one-way redacted record that never carries the value, and resolve() is the internal read that hands the value to a builder and is explicitly not part of the one-way surface. Read precedence is env > file and the env var name IS the ref, so a WRITE on an env-shadowed ref is REJECTED with CredentialShadowedError because a silent shadowed write would make the user believe the file value took effect. Empty/whitespace means 'not configured here' symmetrically (writes reject it, the loader drops such entries, and an empty env var does NOT shadow the file). Reads degrade to empty and never throw; writes are atomic (tmp + rename) with mode 0600 on the temp file plus a defensive chmod. Values at rest are PLAINTEXT in the refs map — the stated protection is file permissions plus atomic replacement, with no encryption and no OS keychain.
invariants: The settings document must never hold key material
describe() never echoes a value
An empty env var does not shadow the file
model.failurePolicy: split: fail-open on READ (a missing file is a normal first run; a corrupt document degrades to empty with a console.warn) and fail-loud on WRITE

extension.name: plugin-event-kernel-with-four-extension-channels
extension.what: The plugin kernel is a scope tree (child scopes via scope.mount) holding a service registry plus FOUR deliberately different extension channels: plain listeners (return values ignored unless a waterfall exists for the event), waterfall (every handler MUST call next(); forgetting throws and double-next throws — no arity heuristics), cascade (around-hooks over one `final`, where skipping next() legally short-circuits and double-next throws) and guards (deny-only string reason). Ancestor composition is explicit and monotonic: guards walk self->root with first-deny-wins so a child allow can never re-allow a parent deny, cascades are collected root-FIRST so ancestor handlers wrap child dispatches outermost, and decisions are nearest-wins. A separate resolveAncestorDecision that skips `self` exists because the per-scope decision map is a shared slot across in-flight emits. Unmount is synchronous reclamation with an async cap: registry removal, nested reclaim and listener/waterfall/cascade deregistration all happen synchronously so a caller that fires ctx.unmount and proceeds immediately sees the plugin gone, and only promise-returning disposers are awaited, raced against a 5 s unref'd timer.
invariants: A waterfall handler that never releases the chain is an error, not a decision (the failure mode being designed out is a silent veto)
A child scope must not be able to escape a root-mounted policy handler
Decision seeding is detection of 'a value was produced', not object identity
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed on protocol violations (forgot/double next, duplicate service registration, unknown service) but fail-open on teardown (a disposer exceeding the 5 s cap logs and the unmount completes anyway)

extension.name: mcp-client-with-generation-based-reconnection-and-oauth
extension.what: An MCP client over stdio or streamable-http that bridges tools/resources into the core-tools registry. Reconnection is GENERATION-based: every reconnect builds a NEW client + transport (a dead transport cannot be reused), transport death calls generationDown under an isCurrent identity check so stale/duplicate notifications are no-ops, backoff is min(maxDelayMs, initialDelayMs * 2^(n-1)), a generation alive >= maxDelayMs resets the attempt budget, and beyond maxRetries the supervisor unregisters ALL of the server's tools and emits state 'lost' exactly once (timers are cleared on close and unref'd). Tool closures bind a stable PROXY that consults `current` at call time and fails fast with McpServerUnavailableError while no generation exists. An overlap guard requires a failing generation to CLOSE within 5 s or reconnecting stops, because two live stdio children for one server is forbidden. Tool sync is two-phase — phase 1 drains all pages (cap 100) and detects blocked tools WITHOUT touching the registry, phase 2 disposes the previous generation's tools then registers the new ones with rollback — and a registry conflict PROPAGATES on initial sync (mount fails closed) but warns and rolls back on a re-sync. Public names are mcp__<server>__<tool>, sanitized and capped at 64 chars with a 12-hex SHA-256 suffix whenever normalization or truncation changed the name (forced when either segment contains '__', which would make the join ambiguous).
invariants: A public tool name must never collapse two distinct (server, tool) identities
A call during an outage errors immediately instead of hanging on a dead transport
A generic 5xx/network error never tears down a healthy generation
extension.failurePolicy: split by phase: startup failure is a MOUNT failure that rejects unless failOnStartupError is false (then it mounts EMPTY with a warning); runtime generation death is fail-soft-but-bounded (retry then 'lost'); registry conflicts are fail-closed on initial sync and fail-soft on re-sync; config validation is fail-loud up front

extension.name: plugin-lifecycle-that-never-executes-plugin-code
extension.what: The host-facing plugin lifecycle registers marketplace sources (local dir, http(s) marketplace.json, owner/repo, git URL), installs/uninstalls plugin packages under <root>/<id>, enables/disables with materialized read-only overlays (skills/, commands/) and re-keyed MCP config, and exposes a catalog plus a pure runtime capability evaluator. Plugin code is NEVER executed by this package and that is confirmed from code, not documentation: manifests, package.json and .mcp.json are only JSON.parsed, commands are only read as markdown, install is a plain file copy, materialize is only rm+cp, and evaluatePlugin is a pure function that pins the `executable` capability dimension to 'unsupported' unconditionally — so a plugin whose ONLY advertised dimension is executable is overall 'failed'. The only process spawned anywhere in the package is `git` for cloning a source (with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and timeouts), which is not plugin code. Entry-source containment is checked TWICE (lexical + realpath) before any copy and the install is a two-phase atomic swap (stage inside installRoot, park the old copy, rename in).
invariants: Not executing plugin code is a property of the host, so an 'executable' capability can never become ready
A broken enable writes NOTHING (no partial enable); a command-name conflict is recorded, not fatal
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed on artifacts and validation (typed install/enable errors leave state untouched or atomically consistent) but fail-CONTINUE-and-loud where a bad input must not break the whole surface (an unreadable source, command file or vanished install dir is warned and skipped)

extension.name: skill-md-deferred-retrieval-with-a-shadow-selector
extension.what: A skill registry scans <workspace>/skills and the global ~/.i-harness/skills root (workspace overrides global), parses YAML front-matter with the real yaml parser, and keeps BODIES DEFERRED: list()/searchSkills() touch summaries only, the BM25 searchable text is exactly name + description with no inputSchema and no searchHint, and getSkill() re-reads the SKILL.md fresh. skill_search is the deferred-retrieval entry and skill_get the explicit body load; both are exposure 'direct' and read-only so the model can DISCOVER skills it does not know exist, and skill_get renders a <skill_content> block with an XML-escaped body, the base directory and a SAMPLED file list marked 'sampled N of M'. Implicit invocation is gated and separately OBSERVED: a deterministic pure shadow selector runs before the real selection (capped at 8 candidates, unioning exact/select matches, real BM25 hits and a lexical substring variant) and emits a skill/selector-shadow telemetry row through an injected emitter without changing behavior; with allowImplicitInvocation false, skill_search returns ONLY explicit mention matches. getSkill distinguishes 'broken' from 'not found' by probing the conventional locations and letting readSkillFile throw a CODED error so the model is told to repair the file rather than misled with SKILL_NOT_FOUND.
invariants: Bodies are loaded only when asked for
One malformed SKILL.md warns and is skipped rather than breaking the registry
extension.failurePolicy: tiered: scan is fail-soft (a missing root is silent, an unreadable directory or a per-skill error warns and skips), explicit requests are fail-closed and loud, and the shadow report never throws

extension.name: lsp-integration-with-one-server-per-run-scheduling
extension.what: A Content-Length-framed JSON-RPC connection over a spawned subprocess with an initialize handshake, a SERIALIZED abortable query queue and transient didOpen/didClose lifecycles. Only Content-Length is parsed and every frame is bounded: the decoder rejects a missing/odd header and an oversized message by throwing, and the connection treats an undecodable frame as stream corruption and fails ALL pending requests. Abort is protocol-level (an already-aborted signal rejects immediately; a later abort sends $/cancelRequest, drops the pending entry and rejects), server->client REQUESTS are always answered (with -32601 if no handler) because JSON-RPC mandates a response or the server hangs, and server->client NOTIFICATIONS are ignored by design (the pull model). Capability gating is fail-closed: an explicit false OR an ABSENT capability key throws LSP_UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION. All queries are serialized on one promise chain and each runs a transient didOpen -> request -> didClose(finally) lifecycle with the file's CURRENT bytes. Teardown is bounded in four steps (shutdown bounded by shutdownTimeoutMs, exit, a kill grace period, then kill escalation) and dispose is idempotent. Mount is ONE server per RUN enforced by a module-level reservation set: a second mount, even with a different name, is a hard error (multi-server is an explicit non-goal) because the tool surface has no server selector; a failed mount disposes the instance and releases the reservation.
invariants: One query at a time; a failed query must not stall later ones
An absent capability is not evidence of support
Dispose never waits forever on a hung server
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed on protocol and capability boundaries (undecodable/oversized frames fail all pending requests, unsupported operations throw, a hung initialize rejects with LSP_INITIALIZE_TIMEOUT, requests on a disposed instance throw); shutdown/exit during dispose and kill on a dead process are best-effort

extension.name: model-facing-hook-and-extension-surfaces-over-the-plugin-seams
extension.what: Beyond the gate/observer semantics, the hook package is the CONFIG surface: handlers are declared in hooks.json (version 1) with an id, a known event, a known type, a non-blank command.cmd, a required 64-hex trust.sha256, a matcher defining tool and/or toolRegex with case-insensitive matching, and an optional positive-integer timeoutMs. Validation is strict (unknown fields throw, wrong types throw, block:true without a reason throws) and the document must be a JSON object with version 1. A re-dispatch guard consumes core-plugin's isCascadeRedispatch so one logical tool call sees exactly one pre-tool/post-tool pair.
invariants: A bad regex is a config error, not a runtime surprise
Only session/start, session/end, subagent/stop and notification are programmatic events; fire() rejects the rest
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed: a missing EXPLICIT config file is a hard HookConfigError while a missing default file yields zero handlers

service.name: web-service-surface-unary-http-routes-one-websocket-mux
service.what: One node:http server serves unary JSON HTTP routes (sessions/workspaces/settings/models/plugins/goal/jobs/feedback/attachments/commands) plus a SINGLE WebSocket mux at /api/mux that multiplexes named live streams (session/chunk/reasoning/agent-state/approval/question/command) addressed by streamId — not per-feature sockets and not SSE. Each open is answered with {type:'ready'} then {type:'item'}... then {type:'end'}, is cancellable by {type:'cancel'}, and approval/question answers ride the same socket as non-open messages keyed by a globally unique id. History is served by the HTTP events route with paging; the live streams deliberately have no replay. The package is transport-only: it maps embedder seams (executor, coordinator, settings, plugin registry, bridges) onto wire shapes and never touches those packages' internals. Live streams are per-session refcounted bundles with gen-forward rebind — a persistence snapshot is never trusted as the live instance, so attachLiveSession() registers the real instance AND re-points already-open generators.
invariants: The launch-token/HMAC-cookie auth is opt-in, but the DNS-rebind/CORS fence is UNCONDITIONAL for every route and the mux upgrade
A single workspace: the execution workspace is fixed at construction and a request cwd never changes it
There is no prompt store: the only queue is the executor's per-session lane
service.failurePolicy: fail-closed at the security boundary (non-loopback Host/Origin -> 403 and socket.destroy() on upgrade, missing/invalid credentials -> 401 before any dispatch) and explicit elsewhere (missing optional seams -> per-route 404, an unexpected throw -> JSON 500 via the owns-the-response catch, an unanswered approval -> {approved:false} on a 30 s timeout)

service.name: external-sdk-stdio-server-with-a-frozen-v0-wire-contract
service.what: One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per NDJSON line over a duplex (stdio): framing is pure (no I/O), malformed lines are silently ignored and never echoed, and request ids echo into responses. protocolVersion is 2 while the v0 FIELD-LEVEL surface (initialize / session/prompt / session/status / shutdown plus the session/event and session/status notifications) is declared FROZEN with a drift sentinel test, and only ADDITIVE changes are allowed without a version bump — protocolVersion stayed 2 across four additive rounds. Host capabilities are advertised as capability ROWS, and a method whose host seam is absent answers -32601/-32603 rather than pretending to work; session/list with no listing source answers an honest blank { sessions: [], listingUnavailable: true }. The server is session-service backed and per-session serialized around ONE AbortController slot per in-flight submit (created before service.submit, cleared in finally only if it still holds this submit's controller). Historical events are never replayed to a fresh subscription — replay/resume is the client's problem via session/history.
invariants: Additive-only versioning: changing or removing an existing shape/field/code requires a version bump
stdout carries ONLY protocol frames (diagnostics go to stderr)
service.failurePolicy: fail-open framing plus fail-closed request semantics: malformed lines are ignored, invalid params/unknown sessions answer -32602 with an explicit 'session not found' (no auto-create), unknown methods -32601, host/engine errors -32603; session/cancel is the deliberate exception and answers {cancelled:false, reason:'not-found'} inside a success payload

service.name: acp-v1-server-for-the-automation-subset
service.what: An Agent Client Protocol v1 server over the official SDK implementing exactly the automation subset: initialize (echoes the SDK PROTOCOL_VERSION and declares sessionCapabilities {list, close, resume}), session/new (coordinator-backed id when a coordinator is given, else a random UUID), session/list (coordinator list UNION sessions created here), session/resume (ownership adopt, unknown ids fail closed), session/close (abort in-flight + closeSession + flush + release ownership), session/prompt and the session/cancel notification. Everything else is a documented v0 drop-set (MCP servers on session/new, per-session cwd execution, session/update mirroring, session/delete, session/fork, set_mode/set_config_option, terminal/fs/elicitation client methods, authentication methods). The permission face is a BINARY switch rather than a round-trip: autoApprove (default true) is allow-once admission and autoApprove false refuses the prompt BEFORE admission, so the session service never sees it — there is no session/request_permission flow in v0. Lifecycle races are handled by an explicit per-session close/generation protocol instead of a lock (closingSessions blocks new prompts and reopening, a monotonic lifecycleGeneration invalidates a suspended resume, concurrent closes share one promise, and a resume that loses the race releases the ownership it just acquired). Only text content blocks are admitted as prompt input.
invariants: The implemented surface is exactly the seven automation methods/notifications
A refused prompt never reaches the session service
service.failurePolicy: fail-closed: unknown/closing sessions throw on resume/prompt/close, autoApprove:false refuses before admission, and an aborted prompt answers stopReason 'cancelled' rather than an error the client might retry

service.name: interaction-seams-approval-answerer-question-provider-ui-command-plane
service.what: The host/engine interaction seams: the approval answerer is NORMALIZED TO A BOOLEAN at registration (async (req) => (await fn(req)).approved) so a host implementing a richer shape can never fail open by returning a truthy object, because core-tools checks `if (!ok) throw`. askUser is deliberately NOT async so a missing question provider throws SYNCHRONOUSLY (NO_PROVIDER) at the call site. One command-name grammar is shared by registration, parsing and listing (^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$, a TypeError at registration), and parseCommandLine parses the same alphabet with an optional leading slash. Commands are a UI plane: dispatched through their own registry in the plugin services map, results returned directly to the caller and NEVER fed into model history; runCommand is fail-loud on an unknown command while listCommands returns [] for a legal empty registry.
invariants: A command result must not become model context
The name grammar must be identical on the registration and parsing sides
service.failurePolicy: fail-closed (a missing question provider throws synchronously, registerCommand throws TypeError on a bad name, runCommand throws on an unknown command, the answerer is boolean-normalized) and fail-open only for discovery/listing

service.name: cli-host-surface-with-a-split-fail-loud-silent-fallback-discipline
service.what: One CLI dispatches to run/web/tui/sdk/acp/sessions over the same engine, and the dispatch is exact equality on args[0] with everything else falling through to the TUI, so an unknown subcommand is not rejected ('i-harness --sandbox x run t' starts the TUI) and no parser supports --flag=value. Fail-loud paths: --session-backend, run --sandbox with a bad value, --resume without a store or id, --model without --api-key, sessions show without an id. Silent-fallback paths: web --port falls through to the PORT env var then to 4310, web --session-dir with a missing value uses the default root, sessions --last with a non-number means 20, an unknown tui --mode is ignored. The two philosophies coexist and their boundary does not align with importance: 'tui --yes' is parsed but never read (it appears only in the parse and in two usage strings, and the TUI has no approval flag), and 'run --help' executes a headless turn whose task is the literal string '--help'.
invariants: Every host builds the SAME engine through createSessionAssembly / createSessionService
service.failurePolicy: mixed and not aligned with importance: security-relevant flags fail loud, presentation flags silently fall back, and unrecognized flags silently become part of the task text or are ignored

retrieval.name: session-search-and-lineage-over-a-rebuildable-sqlite-index
retrieval.what: Full-text session search and lineage over the durable JSONL store, with the store as the SOLE authority: reconcile-on-search snapshots the store (revision dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs), diffs against indexed_sessions, SKIPS unchanged sessions without re-reading the file, and rebuilds changed/removed sessions in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction each (delete + insert docs/lineage + fingerprint). A content fingerprint (sha256 of exactly the bytes that produced the rows) catches stat-only changes and just advances the revision. The index is self-describing and disposable: PRAGMA application_id 'IHQU' + user_version 1, and a version mismatch WITH our own identity resets and rebuilds the derived tables instead of migrating them, while a FOREIGN index is never touched. Query safety is by construction: every whitespace token of the user query becomes a quoted FTS phrase with embedded quotes doubled (so *, OR, NEAR and parentheses are literal text) and the limit is clamped into [1, MAX_LIMIT] with a non-integer rejected. Reconciles are single-flight chained and every opened DatabaseSync is tracked so hosts can release handles on Windows.
invariants: The index is a derivation, never a second truth
Stale rows are never served: a scan/read/decode failure raises a typed error instead of returning partial rows
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-closed (typed SessionQueryError on observe failure, SESSION_QUERY_INDEX_FOREIGN for a foreign/newer index, throws for an unknown session in lineage and for a lineage cycle) with two deliberate fail-open cases (a missing store directory -> empty result; a zero-byte file skipped until its header is written)

retrieval.name: image-attachments-with-an-opaque-id-and-validate-before-publish
retrieval.what: Image attachment persistence plus the model-callable read_image tool: bytes are written under <workspaceDir>/.i-harness/attachments/<opaque-id>.bin behind a validate-before-publish limit check, and read_image turns an on-disk image file into an inline ImageInput (mime + base64) without any store write. The attachment id is opaque and never a filesystem path ('att-<uuid>' maps to the .bin name) so no caller-supplied name can steer the write target and the display name lives only in the returned ref. save() checks the media type against the allowed list and the per-image byte cap BEFORE any mkdir/write, so a rejected upload leaves nothing on disk. read_image is READ-ONLY and returns fs failures instead of throwing (it reuses the fs layer's resolvePath and softFail), because a throwing tool body fails the whole turn, which reads to the model as 'read_image hung'.
invariants: An id from an upload surface is never path-shaped
A partially written attachment (a dangling ref the model could still load) cannot exist
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-closed on save (unsupported media type or oversize throws before any write), fail-loud-but-RETURNED on an unsupported read_image extension; delete() is deliberately best-effort

constants.name: maxImageBytes / maxImagesPerMessage / maxMessageImageBytes / maxImagePixels / maxImageDimension
constants.value: 10 MiB / 4 / 20 MiB / 16 Mi / 8192 (only the first is enforced by save(); the rest are declared and unread)

retrieval.name: session-listing-and-title-derivation-as-a-retrieval-surface
retrieval.what: The retrieval-facing session surfaces are the JSONL list/profile pair plus session-title: a session list needs the header and a blank/content verdict, so profile() answers exactly for artifacts at or under 1024 bytes and honestly-bounded ('may have content, never guessed blank') above that, reading the header from a capped 64 KiB window. Titles are derived from REAL user messages only (any user/message carrying a `source` is excluded so a runtime-context snapshot cannot win the title) with a deterministic word-count fallback, and are persisted BOTH as a session/title log event (latest-wins projection) and as a namespaced document mirror for cheap list screens.
invariants: The log is the truth for resume; the document exists only to make a session list cheap
Auto-titling is idempotent: it returns early when a title already exists or there are no eligible messages
retrieval.failurePolicy: fail-soft throughout: a provider failure degrades to the deterministic fallback and the document mirror write is fired-and-caught

ops.name: host-side-telemetry-stream-with-a-closed-manifest-and-sink-isolation
ops.what: A telemetry stream SEPARATE from the session log and invisible to the agent: a fixed manifest of 20 event codes across 8 domains (session|turn|tool|provider|token|retry|mcp|system), each row carrying a domain and cross-source refs mapping the I-harness codes to the five-source audit's names so vocabulary drift is answered inside the repo while the codes stay stable; the emitted type union is DERIVED from the manifest (single source). createTelemetry multicasts to sinks with per-sink error isolation — a throwing or rejecting sink is warned about and never interrupts the other sinks or the emitting code. The shipped sink is a stdout JSONL sink writing one {ts, type, data} line per event over any WritableStream, so a host can pipe telemetry separately from the session log; close() is a v0 no-op, making flushing the sink's own responsibility. The manifest's `refs` field is what makes a code-without-a-producer detectable (every row has one).
invariants: The telemetry stream is independent of the session log and never enters model context
The event type union is derived from the manifest, so a new code requires a manifest row
ops.failurePolicy: fail-open / fail-visible: sink errors are warned and isolated; close() does not flush

constants.name: event shape
constants.value: { type, ts: Date.now(), data: Record<string, unknown> }

ops.name: per-message-feedback-channel-with-verify-after-write-durability
ops.what: User feedback (like/dislike plus an optional note) is persisted as ONE coordinator document per session keyed 'feedback-<sessionId>' and consumed only by the SPA over the web host's HTTP routes. Per-item optimistic concurrency uses an integer version starting at 1 and incremented per successful put; a put WITHOUT ifVersion overwrites unconditionally (a deliberate divergence from the reference, called out in code) while a mismatched ifVersion is a version conflict carrying `current`, and an identical-value put is a no-op that does not bump the version. The target message identity is the event SEQ of a FINALIZED assistant/message event, VERIFIED against the durable log AFTER a flush (the live instance may hold an event the write-behind has not written yet). Writes VERIFY AFTER WRITE because the coordinator's putDocument contract is report-never-reject: the document is re-read inside the same serialized op and deep-compared with the intended snapshot, and a mismatch throws so the host answers 500 instead of a silent 200 whose vote vanishes on refresh. All read-modify-write cycles, reads included, are serialized on one promise chain whose tail survives failures.
invariants: A write is never acknowledged before it is verified
A feedback messageId must name a real assistant/message in the durable log
ops.failurePolicy: fail-closed on durability (an unverifiable write throws FeedbackPersistenceError -> 500) and on input (typed machine-coded errors mapped to HTTP statuses without string matching: invalid/note-blank/note-too-large/message-not-found -> 400, version-conflict -> 409, unknown session -> 404); cheap-field validation runs BEFORE any session load

ops.name: settings-document-layered-precedence-hot-reload-comment-preservation
ops.what: The global/layered settings document is the single source for every setting. Layer precedence is global < workspace < project (later wins), merged as RAW documents deep per key with arrays/scalars replaced and normalized ONCE, so unknown keys survive as long as a higher layer does not override them; writes go to the MASTER = the highest-priority EXISTING source, so a project file that does not exist is never created by a write aimed at the global file. Hot reload is a dependency-free POLLING watcher on mtime+size (default 500 ms, unref'd timer; polling chosen over fs events deliberately to avoid new dependencies) whose first tick only snapshots, and which MERGES a change-detection gate before notifying so listeners fire only when the NORMALIZED view actually changed. Comments are preserved on write with three ordered strategies (exact positional re-anchoring, anchor-by-surviving-line, and a DEGRADED preservation that keeps leading/trailing blocks and relocates interior extras) and a document the comment parser cannot read at all is left untouched with a thrown error. The section API is a validated leaf-patch protocol with a per-section _revision counter guarding expectedRevision (a stale value throws a conflict), there is deliberately NO migration chain (legacy shapes soft-upgrade at read), and cross-process concurrent writes are explicitly accepted as last-rename-wins.
invariants: Merging happens on RAW documents so unknown keys survive
Degradation never deletes user data; a write is fail-closed on an unparsable document
Inline comments inside values are unsupported (fail-closed rather than corrupt)
ops.failurePolicy: fail-closed on writes (SettingsPatchError, SettingsValidationError -> 400, SettingsConflictError -> 409) and non-throwing on reads (malformed values degrade to defaults)

interface.name: tui-event-stream-contract-over-the-session-log
interface.what: The backend interface a renderer consumes is the session-log subscription mapped onto a renderer event vocabulary: the embedded bridge calls createSessionService and subscribes to core-session, mapping user/message -> user, assistant/chunk -> assistant, reasoning -> thinking, tool/call + tool/result -> tool (with toolKindOf), plus turn/start|end, compaction/*, todo/write, goal/change, session/title, plan/mode and command/run|done -> system. The mapping batches at 16 ms and carries the session-log seq as the cursor so a renderer can replay(afterSeq) through the deriveMessages/events line. The bridge is embedded-first: the SDK subprocess and --attach path reuse the same frozen consumer surface.
invariants: The renderer's cursor is the session-log seq; batching never reorders events
The event vocabulary is a mapping of the log, so a renderer can always re-derive state from the log alone
interface.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a missing optional backend member resolves to a toast or an honest empty panel rather than an exception in the render loop

interface.name: hard-slash-command-capability-gate
interface.what: The command surface is gated by a typed SlashCapability union derived at runtime from REAL backend/host members, and the gate is HARD rather than a UI filter: visible(ctx)===false makes a command neither listed by completionEntries() nor matched by matches(), and an unmatched slash line renders 'Unsupported command: /<name>' and never reaches the backend. Loop.slashCapabilities() pushes only session-list, session-create, dashboard, rewind, compact, fork, context and provider-settings, so plan-mode, guardian and vim-mode are NEVER pushed and /plan, /view-plan, /auto, /always-approve and /vim-mode are unreachable in the shipped TUI by construction (their run bodies are single toasts). Three commands bypass the registry table entirely: /settings, /provider and /model are intercepted earlier in the submit path by a text modal check, and their registry entries are only the inventory/forwarding surface. Commands whose SlashContext member is optional guard on presence and toast rather than no-op.
invariants: A capability that is never pushed makes its commands unreachable, not merely hidden
A command must be reachable through its registered run body or explicitly documented as a stub
interface.failurePolicy: fail-closed at the gate: an uncapable or unmatched command is refused before it can become a user prompt

constants.name: SlashCapability vocabulary
constants.value: session-create | session-list | dashboard | provider-settings | rewind | compact | fork | context | plan-mode | guardian | vim-mode

constants.name: capabilities actually pushed
constants.value: session-list, session-create, dashboard, rewind, compact, fork, context, provider-settings (8 of 11)

interface.name: screen-mode-policy-and-host-re-launch-seam
interface.what: Fullscreen / minimal screen mode is a HOST-LEVEL policy rather than a renderer concern: the slash commands forward the raw line to TuiAppOptions.modeSwitch on the host relay, which respawns the process in the requested mode and reports whether it spawned, and the loop quits the current process only when the host confirms the spawn happened. The COMPACT layout flag is likewise a host/app option threaded into the layout and view-description builders (layoutAgent takes { compact }), not a backend capability. Capability detection is exposed to the interface as a probe report surface that a host can implement or omit, with the missing-seam path rendering an honest empty panel.
invariants: A mode switch that the host did not perform must not terminate the current process
Layout/mode flags are host options, not engine state
interface.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a missing modeSwitch/probeReport seam degrades to a toast or an empty panel
